I am 63 this year, and I have farmed in Quzhou County for 40 years. I never went to school. I learned everything from my mother and from watching my neighbors. My land is 12.4 mu. I keep 2 mu of cotton on the east side, the same plot we always had. The other 10.4 mu I plant winter wheat in October, and the moment the wheat comes off in early June I put summer maize in. That is my system.

For the wheat: After the maize stalks are chopped, I will run the rotary tiller over the field. I buy the improved wheat seed from the dealer in town, about 15 kg for each mu. Before sowing I spread half a 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on every mu. Then when the wheat wakes up in March and starts growing fast, I spread urea on top — about 30 jin for each mu. I would rather put a little too much than too little; if the harvest fails I have nothing, but wasting some fertilizer is only a few yuan lost. I water three times: once before winter if the ground is dry, once when the wheat is shooting up tall, and once when the grain is getting plump. I spray twice — herbicide right after sowing, and once more if I see bugs. Last year I got about 500 kg from each mu, and I think I will get that again.

For the summer maize: Right after we cut the wheat, I plant the hybrid maize seed straight into the stubble without ploughing again. There is no time, and the soil is soft enough. At planting I put about 20 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows. When the corn is knee-high I spread 25 jin of urea per mu. I water once in July, and only a second time if the sun is very hot and the leaves curl. One spray for weeds is usually enough. I expect about 600 kg per mu.

For the cotton: This is the hardest work. I plough and rotary till the 2 mu in spring. I plant the hybrid cotton seed and cover the rows with plastic film to keep the ground warm. Cotton eats a lot. I put one full 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on each mu when I plant. When the flowers come I add about 25 jin of urea per mu. I water twice, once when it flowers and once when the bolls are swelling. I spray three times because the cotton worms and red spiders always come. Picking hurts my back, so I hire two women from the village for several days. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton from each mu. My neighbor uses the same amounts, so I do not change.

Everything costs money — seed, fertilizer, diesel for the pump, the hired pickers. I think about the whole year at once. If fertilizer prices went up too much I might use a little less on the maize, but for now I will do what I did last year. Change is risky.
